Exhaustive local 10-vertex case analysis has 24 relative faces; the explicitly listed twelve free-face pairs are directly checked as the unique strict cofaces in sequence. Lifting one certificate to each of the n−4 disjoint fibers is an elementary-collapse proof for every n>=5. Standalone graph-based verifier checks the local certificate and all faces at n=5,6,7 (261→285, 747→795, 1751→1823), with no numerical extrapolation required. The proof establishes a simple-homotopy equivalence and integral isomorphism, not an unsupported independent homotopy computation.

value.rationale: Two-independence Kneser complexes encode dissociation/induced-P3-free set systems, with previously established nontrivial three-sphere bouquet topology and an integral symmetry module. Deleting even one disjointness relation introduces an unbounded number 24(n−4) of admissible faces, so it is mathematically nonobvious whether topological classes or the natural inclusion survive. The theorem provides a uniform constructive and linear-length simple-homotopy stability certificate, stronger than comparing Betti ranks or individual intact homotopy types, for every pair-Kneser graph. This isolates a useful mechanism for fault stability, not a small arbitrary finite recomputation.
